grammar.title: XはYです
grammar.explanation: Basic equational sentence pattern meaning "X is Y / As for X, it is Y." Japanese speakers frequently omit the topic/subject (`がくせいです。` — "(I) am a student") whenever it is clear from context.
bulletPoints: **Topic particle `は`:** Written with hiragana `は` (`ha`) following classical orthography, but pronounced `wa` when marking a topic (and in `こんにちは`, `こんばんは`).
**No articles or plurals:** Japanese nouns stand alone without "a/an/the" or plural `-s`, so `がくせいです` can mean "am a student" or "are students" depending on context.

grammar.title: Question Sentences
grammar.explanation: Add the question particle `か` at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no or question-word question (it is not customary to write a `?` in standard Japanese).
bulletPoints: **Question words:** `なん / なに` (what), `なんじ` (what time), `なんさい` (how old), `なんねんせい` (what year in school), `なんばん` (what number).
**`なん` vs. `なに`:** Use `なん` immediately before `です` (`なんですか`) or counters like `じ`, `さい`, `ねんせい`, `ばん`; use `なに` before particles or in `なにじん` (what nationality).

grammar.title: Noun₁ の Noun₂
grammar.explanation: The particle `の` connects two nouns, where `Noun₂` is the **main idea** and `Noun₁` restricts, specifies, or shows possession (`Takeshi's`). A `Noun₁ の Noun₂` phrase acts like one big noun.
bulletPoints: Pattern: Noun₁ の Noun₂ (Noun₂ of Noun₁ / Noun₁'s Noun₂).
Can denote ownership: 私の本 (my book), メアリーさんの傘 (Mary's umbrella).
Can denote affiliation: さくら大学の学生 (student of Sakura University).

grammar.title: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
grammar.pattern: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
grammar.explanation: Standalone demonstrative pronouns ("this one / that one / that one over there / which one?") used directly before `は` or `が`.
bulletPoints: **Distance:** `これ` (near speaker), `それ` (near listener), `あれ` (far from both), `どれ` (which one).
**Question-word particle rule:** `どれ` cannot be followed by `は`; always use `が` (`どれですか` / `どれがあなたのペンですか`).
**Politeness rule:** Do not use `これ / それ / あれ` to introduce people within earshot (`*これはメアリーさんです`).

grammar.title: Verb Conjugation (Present Tense Affirmative & Negative)
grammar.explanation: Japanese verbs are sorted into three conjugation classes: **ru-verbs**, **u-verbs**, and **irregular verbs**. Dictionary forms are used in dictionary entries and casual contexts, while present-tense polite forms replace the ending with `-ます` (affirmative) and `-ません` (negative).
bulletPoints: **Ru-verbs:** Base ends with `e` or `i` + `る` (`食べる` = `tabe + ru`). Drop `る` and add `ます` / `ません` (`食べます` / `食べません`, `寝ます` / `寝ません`, `起きます` / `起きません`, `見ます` / `見ません`).
**U-verbs:** Consonant-final base + `u` (`飲む` = `nom + u`). Replace `u` with `imasu` / `imasen` (`飲みます`, `読みます`, `話します`, `聞きます`, `行きます`).

**Trap `-eru` / `-iru` u-verbs:** Verbs ending in `-aru`, `-oru`, or `-uru` are always u-verbs, while some `-eru`/`-iru` verbs like `帰る` (`kaer + u` → `帰ります`, NOT `*帰ます`) are also u-verbs. Memorize each verb as a set (e.g., `行く — 行きます`).
**Irregular verbs:** `する` → `します / しません`, `勉強する` → `勉強します / 勉強しません`, `くる` → `きます / きません`.

grammar.title: Core Particles (`を`, `で`, `に`, `へ`)
grammar.explanation: Nouns in sentences are followed by particles indicating their grammatical relation to the verb (in casual speech, particles are sometimes dropped).
bulletPoints: **`を` (pronounced *o*):** Marks the direct object directly involved in or affected by the verb.
**`で`:** Marks the place where an action/event takes place.

**`に`:** Marks (1) the goal toward which things move (with verbs like `行く`, `来る`, `帰る`), and (2) the specific time at which an event takes place. For approximate time, substitute `ごろ` or `ごろに` for `に`.
**`へ` (pronounced *e*):** Marks the goal of movement and can replace directional `に` with `行く`, `来る`, `帰る`, but **cannot** replace `に` for time references.

grammar.title: Time Reference Rules with `に`
grammar.explanation: Whether a time expression takes the particle `に` depends on the category of the time word.
bulletPoints: **Requires `に`:** Days of the week (`日曜日に`) and numerical time expressions (`十時四十五分に`, `九月に`).
**Never takes `に`:** Relative time expressions (`今日`, `あした`, `きのう`), regular intervals (`毎日`, `毎晩`), and the question word `いつ`.
**Optional `に`:** Parts of the day (`朝(に)`, `夜(に)`) and `週末(に)`, depending on style and emphasis.

grammar.title: Existence & Possession (`Xがあります / います`)
grammar.pattern: Xがあります / います
grammar.explanation: Use `あります` (for non-living things, possessions, and scheduled events) and `います` (for people and living, moving things) to express "there is/are X."
bulletPoints: **Location & existence:** `[Place に] + [Thing が あります / Person が います]`. Notice the place takes `に` (not `で`), except when `あります` means an **event taking place** (`京都でお祭りがあります`).
**Possession:** `[Thing が あります / ありません]` means "to have / not have" (`テレビがありません`). Contrast with `テレビじゃありません` ("It isn't a TV").
**Colloquial negative of `ある`:** `ないです` (never `*あらないです`).
**Note on `います/あります` vs. `です`:** `います/あります` describe existence or location (`あそこに留学生がいます`), whereas `です` describes an attribute (`メアリーさんは留学生です`).

grammar.title: Adjectives (Present Tense)
grammar.explanation: Japanese has two adjective classes: **`い`-adjectives** and **`な`-adjectives**, each with its own conjugation pattern.
bulletPoints: **`い`-adjectives:** Affirmative adds `です` (`さむいです`). Negative replaces final `い` with `くないです` or `くありません` (`さむくないです` — never `*さむいじゃないです`).
**`な`-adjectives:** Affirmative adds `です` without `な` (`元気です`). Negative replaces `です` with `じゃないです` / `じゃありません` / `ではありません` (`元気じゃないです`).
**Irregular `いい` (good):** Changes `い` to `よ` in all non-dictionary forms (`いいです` → `よくないです` / `よくありません`, `かっこよくないです`). Note: `かわいい` is regular (`かわいくないです`).
**Degree adverbs:** Place `すごく` (extremely), `とても` (very), or `ちょっと` (a little) before adjectives.

grammar.explanation: `好き(な)` (like) and `きらい(な)` (dislike) are `な`-adjectives taking the pattern `Xは Yが 好き／きらいです`.

grammar.title: Verb `て`-form Conjugation
grammar.explanation: The `て`-form is used for requests, connecting actions, permission, and prohibition.
bulletPoints: **`Ru`-verbs:** Drop `る` + `て` (`食べる` → `食べて`).
**`U`-verbs (5 sub-rules):**
`う / つ / る` → `って` (`会う` → `会って`, `待つ` → `待って`, `とる` → `とって`; includes `-iru/-eru` u-verbs like `帰る`, `入る`, `知る`, `いる`, `切る`, `走る`).
`む / ぶ / ぬ` → `んで` (`読む` → `読んで`, `遊ぶ` → `遊んで`, `死ぬ` → `死んで`).
`く` → `いて` (`書く` → `書いて`), **Exception:** `行く` → `行って`.
**Irregular verbs:** `する` → `して`, `くる` → `きて`. Note that `u`-verb `て`-forms differ completely from their `-ます` stems (`書きます` vs. `書いて`).

grammar.title: Short Forms (Present Tense Affirmative & Negative)
grammar.explanation: Short forms (plain/informal forms) are used among close friends/family and inside embedded clauses (`〜と思います`, `〜と言っていました`, `〜のが好き`).
bulletPoints: **Present Affirmative:** Verbs = dictionary form (`読む`); `い`-adj = drop `です` (`かわいい`); `な`-adj & Nouns = replace `です` with `だ` (`静かだ`, `学生だ`).
**Present Negative:**
`Ru`-verbs: drop `る` + `ない` (`食べる` → `食べない`).
`U`-verbs: change final `-u` to `-anai` (`書く` → `書かない`). **Verbs ending in `う` take `わ`** (`会う` → `会わない`, `買う` → `買わない`).
Irregular: `する` → `しない`, `くる` → `こない`, `ある` → `ない` (exception!).
`い`-adj: drop `です` (`かわいくない`, `いい` → `よくない`).
`な`-adj & Nouns: drop `です` (`静かじゃない`, `学生じゃない`).

grammar.title: Short Forms in Informal Speech
grammar.explanation: Close friends and family use short forms to show intimacy, while long forms maintain polite distance. Never use short forms toward social superiors (e.g., professors) even if they use short forms with you.

grammar.title: Past Tense Short Forms (`〜た / 〜なかった`)
grammar.explanation: Only three rules generate all past-tense short forms:
bulletPoints: **Verbs (affirmative):** Replace `て / で` in the `て`-form with `た / だ` (`食べて` → `食べた`, `読んで` → `読んだ`).
**`い`-adjectives (affirmative):** Drop `です` from the past long form (`かわいかった`).
**`な`-adjectives & Nouns (affirmative):** Replace `でした` with `だった` (`静かだった`, `学生だった`).
**All categories (negative):** Replace final `い` in the present negative short form (`〜ない`) with `かった` (`読まなかった`, `かわいくなかった`, `静かじゃなかった`, `学生じゃなかった`).

grammar.title: Explanatory Predicate (`〜んです / 〜のです`)
grammar.explanation: Attach `んです` (written/formal `のです`, casual `んだ` / questions `の`) to a **short form** to provide or ask for an explanation connecting a fact to the current context. When following a present-tense affirmative **noun or `な`-adjective**, insert `な` (`静かなんです`, `学生なんです`).

grammar.title: Obligation / Necessity (`〜なければいけません / 〜なきゃいけません`)
grammar.pattern: 〜なければいけません / 〜なきゃいけません
grammar.explanation: Express "must / have to" by taking the negative short form, dropping final `い`, and adding `ければいけません` (more formal/written) or `きゃいけません` (colloquial/spoken). Past tense uses `いけませんでした`; casual speech shortens to `〜なきゃいけない` or just `〜なきゃ`. (Variants: `〜なければなりません`, `〜ないと／なくてはいけません`.)

grammar.title: Tentative Questions & Guesses (`〜でしょうか / 〜でしょう`)
grammar.explanation: Attach `でしょうか` to short forms (drop `だ` after present affirmative nouns/`な`-adjectives: `野菜でしょうか`, never `*野菜だでしょうか`) to ask polite, tentative questions without putting the listener on the spot. Non-interrogative `でしょう` (often with `たぶん`) expresses a guess ("probably"); casual rising `でしょ？` seeks confirmation ("..., right?").

dialogues.setting: Mary and Yui are talking at school.

lines.ja: メアリーさん、元気がありませんね。
lines.speaker: Yui
lines.en: You don't look well, Mary.

lines.ja: うーん。ちょっとおなかが痛いんです。
lines.speaker: Mary
lines.en: Um ... I have a little stomachache.

lines.ja: どうしたんですか。
lines.speaker: Yui
lines.en: What's the matter?

lines.ja: きのう友だちと晩ご飯を食べに行ったんです。たぶん食べすぎたんです。

lines.ja: 病院に行ったほうがいいですよ。

dialogues.setting: Next day Mary is at a hospital.

lines.ja: 先生、おなかが痛くて熱もあるんです。インフルエンザでしょうか。
lines.speaker: Mary
lines.en: Doctor, I have a stomachache and have a fever, too. Have I got the flu?

lines.ja: インフルエンザじゃないですね。かぜです。
lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: I don't think that you've got the flu. It is just a cold.

lines.ja: よかった。あのう、もうすぐテニスの試合があるので、練習しなきゃいけないんですが……。
lines.speaker: Mary
lines.en: Good. Well, I will have a tennis tournament soon, so I have to practice, though ...

lines.ja: 二三日、運動しないほうがいいでしょう。
lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: You had better not exercise for a couple of days.

lines.ja: わかりました。
lines.speaker: Mary
lines.en: I understand.

lines.ja: 今日は薬を飲んで、早く寝てください。
lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Take medicine and go to bed early tonight.

lines.ja: はい、ありがとうございました。
lines.speaker: Mary
lines.en: Yes. Thank you so much.

lines.ja: お大事に。
lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.en: Take care.
